title: Get 32GB of DDR5 RAM for $111 in this premium AM5 gaming bundle from Newegg
content: Newegg’s freshest Black Friday combo deal takes $369 off four premium PC components, including the Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 32GB DDR5-6000 RAM, Asus ROG Strix X870E-E motherboard, 2TB Samsung SSD, and a free MSI AIO for just $1,549.

title: Phison details SSD with a built-in NPU and 64GB of memory that supports AI frameworks on the drive
content: Phison showed a computational-storage SSD with an NPU and 64GB of memory, plus Mixed Media pSLC and QLC drives, at SC26.

title: Thousands of vulnerable fridges patched against cyberattacks in secret operation
content: Following devastating hacks that caused European fridges to reach 50 degrees Celsius, destroying food stocks, the U.K. has implemented nationwide patching to ensure similar attacks won't affect its fridges.

content: A lawyer’s private AI server now runs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on 12 used Nvidia V100 GPUs, with every expert at 4-bit NVFP4.

title: MSI EdgeMesa N AI+ review: RTX Spark power comes to Windows on Arm desktops, but there are trade-offs
content: MSI's EdgeMesa N AI+ brings Nvidia RTX Spark N1X power to a Windows-on-Arm mini PC with 128GB of unified memory, strong local AI performance, and the ability to game on the side. But its high $7,499 price isn't that much cheaper than more versatile DGX Spark systems.

title: Power and cooling limits force AI clusters with 100,000+ accelerators to use multiple data centers
content: Faster GPUs are no longer enough as power constraints, network congestion, and communication overhead force the industry to rethink how massive AI systems are built.

title: Autonomous 5-ton John Deere skid-steer loader trained to perform acrobatic maneuvers using AI
content: Videos of an incredibly acrobatic, nimble, and graceful John Deere 332G 5-tonne skid-steer loader have been shared by a group of researchers from the U.S. and Switzerland.

title: Taiwan market plunges 6.23% as AI suppliers report steady orders after Huang's exit
content: Taiwan's benchmark Taiex plunged 2,393.60 points, or 6.23%, on Friday to close at 36,033.29, its third-largest single-day point drop on record. Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) fell as low as NT$1,970(US$59.73) before closing at NT$2,000, down 4.76%. MediaTek and Delta Electronics closed at their daily downside limits.

title: TSMC says it will comply with new US rule that strips Chinese chip designers of a key exemption
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) said it will comply with new US export rules that remove a route Chinese chip designers had used to get advanced chips made at overseas foundries without a license. The rule reaches beyond AI processors.

title: Huang's exit tests Nvidia's annual chip cadence and Taiwan suppliers' customer mix
content: Nvidia's decision not to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive has raised concerns about a potential slowdown in AI hardware upgrades, putting Taiwanese suppliers' capacity allocation and order mix across major customers under scrutiny.

title: AI data center construction demand holds firm despite labor shortages as Acter's order backlog reaches NT$84 billion
content: Recent reports suggesting a slowdown in AI data center construction, alongside adjustments to investment and project schedules by some companies, have raised concerns that demand for AI infrastructure may be cooling.

title: Taiwan chip distributors see supply-chain risks after Huang's exit
content: Taiwanese chip distributors expect Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO to cause short-term uncertainty across the company's supply chain, with potential changes in supplier priorities and mounting pressure from US export controls and national security concerns. They do not expect the disruption to derail long-term AI demand.

title: Pan-International targets 2027 optical connector and humanoid robot motor launches
content: Pan-International Industrial Corp. is targeting initial shipments of high-density MMC optical-fiber connectors in the first quarter of 2027 and plans to launch motors for humanoid robots in the third quarter of 2027. The Taiwan-based manufacturer is expanding into AI infrastructure, optical communications and advanced motors as it seeks to offset pressure on its traditional automotive wiring-harness business.

title: US AI chip curbs force Alibaba to rethink overseas compute strategy
content: Alibaba plans to increase its reliance on domestically developed AI chips as tighter US restrictions on overseas computing services threaten China's access to advanced Nvidia GPUs. CEO Eddie Wu acknowledged that regulatory uncertainty could weigh on cloud growth in 2027, while proprietary T-Head processors may eventually support the company's overseas operations.

title: DIGITIMES Insight: US AI chip curbs target computing dominance, Megaspeed clouds Nvidia's future
content: The US is extending its AI export restrictions beyond chips to overseas computing services, tightening China's access to advanced GPUs while strengthening American cloud providers' competitive position. In the latest episode of the DIGITIMES podcast Luke's Talk Room, hosted by senior analyst Luke Lin, the discussion also examines Nvidia's leadership turmoil, persistent AI computing shortages, and the risk of a supply-chain price correction after 2028.

title: Rayzher, Messer form JV for semiconductor specialty gases
content: Rayzher Industrial and German industrial gas supplier Messer signed a joint venture and strategic alliance agreement on November 19 to establish Messer Rayzher Electronic Materials Co. The new business will combine Messer's electronic-grade gas products, manufacturing technology and global supply chain with Rayzher's engineering and local operating capabilities to serve Taiwan's semiconductor market and support overseas expansion.

title: AAEON targets semiconductors, robotics and defense beyond consumer AI inflation
content: Industrial PC maker AAEON Technology reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of NT$2.873 billion (US$87.46 million), up 24.6% year on year, as AI edge computing and embedded products drove core operations, and investment valuation gains boosted non-operating income. Net income attributable to owners of the parent for the first three quarters of 2026 reached NT$1.163 billion, with EPS of NT$9.25.

title: Suregiant targets high-double-digit growth as release film enters advanced packaging
content: AI chips are driving foundries and OSAT providers to expand capacity for advanced packaging technologies such as CoWoS, creating a new wave of localization opportunities for critical materials suppliers. Suregiant Technology's release films have entered mass production for 2.5D, 3D and fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) processes, with shipments expected to maintain at least high-double-digit growth in 2026 and 2027.

title: Global PCB shortage deepens as AI demand strains supplies, with relief unlikely before mid-2028
content: A global shortage of printed circuit boards (PCBs), essential to nearly all consumer electronics, is causing or threatening delivery delays of weeks to months across the automotive, medical, defence and aerospace industries, according to a new warning from the Global Electronics Association.

title: SK Hynix reportedly plans to buy HBM bonding tools from Besi
content: SK Hynix plans to buy its initial batch of hybrid bonding equipment for next-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM) from Dutch chip equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi), potentially giving the company an edge over South Korean rivals competing for orders in advanced memory packaging.

title: Blacklisted Chinese server maker reportedly kept using AMD firmware
content: A Chinese server maker continued using updated AMD firmware after being placed on a US export blacklist, according to an investigation published November 19 that the chipmaker has disputed.
